papers.title: Meta-Learning Conjugate Priors for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian Optimization is methodology used in statistical modelling that utilizes a Gaussian process prior distribution to iteratively update a posterior distribution towards the true distribution of the data. Finding unbiased informative priors to sample from is challenging and can greatly influence the outcome on the posterior distribution if only few data are available. In this paper we propose a novel approach to utilize meta-learning to automate the estimation of informative conjugate prior distributions given a distribution class. From this process we generate priors that require only few data to estimate the shape parameters of the original distribution of the data.

summary_en.motivation: To automate the estimation of informative conjugate priors for Bayesian optimization when data is scarce.
summary_en.method: A meta-learning approach that learns to estimate shape parameters of conjugate prior distributions from related tasks.
summary_en.result: The meta-learned priors enable effective Bayesian optimization with only a few observations.
summary_en.validation: Validated on numerical benchmarks and synthetic data without real-world experimental validation.

papers.title: Phase Transitions in Recovery of Structured Signals from Corrupted Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of recovering a structured signal from a relatively small number of corrupted random measurements. Sharp phase transitions have been numerically observed in practice when different convex programming procedures are used to solve this problem. This paper is devoted to presenting theoretical explanations for these phenomenons by employing some basic tools from Gaussian process theory. Specifically, we identify the precise locations of the phase transitions for both constrained and penalized recovery procedures. Our theoretical results show that these phase transitions are determined by some geometric measures of structure, e.g., the spherical Gaussian width of a tangent cone and the Gaussian (squared) distance to a scaled subdifferential. By utilizing the established phase transition theory, we further investigate the relationship between these two kinds of recovery procedures, which also reveals an optimal strategy (in the sense of Lagrange theory) for choosing the tradeoff parameter in the penalized recovery procedure. Numerical experiments are provided to verify our theoretical results.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究与结构信号的恢复问题，与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA simulation efficiency, surrogate modeling for engineering design, or any biomechanical context; it is purely about signal recovery and phase transitions in compressed sensing.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究在少量被破坏的随机测量中恢复结构信号的问题，并解释凸优化方法中的相变现象。
summary_zh.method: 利用高斯过程理论中的几何度量（如切锥的高斯宽度）推导相变的精确位置。
summary_zh.result: 确定了约束和惩罚恢复过程的相变边界，并揭示了惩罚参数的最优选择策略。
summary_zh.validation: 通过数值实验验证相变理论的预测结果。

summary_en.motivation: The paper investigates the problem of recovering structured signals from corrupted measurements and aims to provide theoretical explanations for observed sharp phase transitions in convex recovery procedures.
summary_en.method: Using tools from Gaussian process theory, the authors identify precise phase transition locations based on geometric measures such as the spherical Gaussian width of tangent cones and Gaussian distance to scaled subdifferentials.
summary_en.result: Theoretical results characterize phase transitions for both constrained and penalized recovery, and reveal an optimal strategy for selecting the tradeoff parameter via Lagrange theory.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on synthetic data verify the theoretical phase transition predictions.

summary_en.motivation: To achieve reproducible fabrication of trabecular bone-mimicking porous structures via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting of Ti6Al4V extra-low interstitials powder to produce porous scaffolds replicating trabecular bone architecture.
summary_en.result: The replicated structures exhibited good reproducibility and mechanical properties comparable to natural trabecular bone.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical characterization via quasi-static compression tests on fabricated samples.
